title: Morera theorem
section: Complex Variables ▷ Theorems Concerning Analytic Functions
terms: Morera theorem; vanishing triangle integrals; analyticity from integration; local uniform convergence.

exposition.text:
Morera’s theorem states that a continuous function on an open set is holomorphic if its integral
around every triangle whose closed interior lies in the set is zero. Requiring every closed con-
tour to have zero integral is a stronger sufficient assumption. Continuity is part of the theorem.
This converts integral information into differentiability. One application is that a function con-
tinuous across a line and holomorphic on both sides is holomorphic across the line: divide tri-
angles along the line, apply Cauchy’s theorem on each side, and pass to the boundary using
continuity. Vanishing on a single contour is insufficient.
Uniform convergence on every compact subset is called local uniform convergence. Such a limit
of holomorphic functions is holomorphic: it is continuous, and uniform convergence on each
fixed triangle boundary permits passing the limit through the contour integral. Morera then
supplies the derivative property without assuming convergence of derivatives in advance.

solution.text:
H
2 2
On the unit circle, |z| = 1, so the integral is dz = 0. But |z| is complex differentiable
only at zero and hence is not entire. The other four choices are entire. Morera requires zero
integrals for every qualifying triangle, not just one chosen closed curve.

question.text:
A function f : C → C is continuous everywhere and holomorphic wherever Im z ̸= 0. Which
must be true?
(A) f is constant.
(B) f is entire.
(C) f is a polynomial.
(D) f is bounded.
(E) f vanishes on the real axis.

solution.text:
Split any triangle crossing the real axis into pieces above and below it. Cauchy’s theorem,
continuity at the line, and cancellation of the shared segments show the boundary integral
is zero. Morera then gives holomorphy on all of C.

question.text:
A continuous function f on an open disk has zero integral around the boundary of every trian-
gle contained in the disk. Which conclusion follows?
(A) f is analytic on the disk.
(B) f is constant.
(C) f is real valued.
(D) f extends to an entire function.
(E) f is a polynomial.

solution.text:
These are precisely the local hypotheses of Morera’s theorem, which yields analyticity.
They impose no polynomial or constant restriction, nor do they guarantee extension
beyond the disk.

solution.text:
Local uniform convergence gives continuity of f and convergence of integrals along each
fixed triangle boundary. Each integral of f is zero, so the integral of f is zero. Morera’s
n
theorem now gives analyticity.

question.text:
Define f(0) = 1 and f(z) = 0 for z ̸= 0. Its integral around every triangle is zero. Why does
Morera’s theorem not imply that f is analytic?
(A) Morera’s theorem applies only to polynomials.
(B) Triangle integrals must equal one.
(C) The domain is not simply connected.
(D) The required continuity hypothesis fails.
(E) The function is unbounded.

solution.text:
The function is discontinuous at zero. Changing an integrand at a single point does not
affect these ordinary contour integrals, but Morera’s theorem requires continuity on the
domain. Thus the integral condition alone does not suffice.
